units.text: INT. PRESBYTERY KITCHEN - 1347 - EARLY MORNING
A low stone room.
Smoke blackens the beams.
A pot of barley hangs over the fire.
BROTHER AUGUSTINE (50s, tonsured, gentle) stirs.
Beside him, SISTER HILDEGARD (40s, wimple, strong forearms) kneads dough on a board.
At the table, an old monk, BROTHER BERNARD (70s, blind, hands folded), listens.
By the door, a servant boy, ELIAS (12, ragged smock), hugs a bundle of firewood.
The harvest is poor.
units.name: AUGUSTINE

units.text: The harvest is always poor.
units.name: HILDEGARD

units.text: It was better when I could see it.
units.name: BERNARD

units.text: Brother, you could not see it then.
units.name: AUGUSTINE

units.text: I could see it in my mind.
units.name: BERNARD

units.text: That is not seeing.
units.name: HILDEGARD

units.text: It is the only kind that lasts.
units.name: BERNARD

units.text: Elias sets the firewood down near the hearth, careful not to wake the embers.
He glances at the pot.
Hildegard breaks off a piece of dough, rolls it, and sets it in his hand without looking.
Thank you, Sister.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: Eat it before the prior sees.
units.name: HILDEGARD

units.text: Augustine tastes the barley and nods.
Bernard breathes in the smoke and the yeast, the old man's face softening.
